answer: Give each agent one bonded identity that earns trust only through completed work. A newcomer has a ferrous cap on trade size, so it handles only tiny jobs. Its cedar reputation grows slowly with honest deliveries and falls fast after fraud, and every deal is written to a marble public ledger peers can audit. Identical behaviour across many fake agents becomes visible, and each copy needs its own bond, fees and waiting time. An attacker must therefore pay repeatedly and risk losing every deposit, making a large fake crowd far costlier than any profit it could steal.
